questions.prompt: A VM has a Standard public IP, a running HTTPS listener, and a guest firewall allowing TCP 443. Its effective NSG rules deny inbound Internet traffic. What must change to accept HTTPS from an approved client range?

options.text: Add an NSG allow rule for that range and TCP 443.
options.explanation: Standard public IP access still requires an NSG permit.

options.text: Set public IP allocation to dynamic.
options.explanation: Standard uses static allocation; allocation does not authorize traffic.

options.text: Add a DNS label to the public IP.
options.explanation: A DNS name does not override the NSG deny.

options.text: Create a second public IP for the NIC.
options.explanation: Another address does not remove the filtering rule.

questions.prompt: You delete a Standard public IP resource and recreate a resource with the same name. What can you rely on?

options.text: Azure restores the old numeric address.
options.explanation: Deletion releases it; the old address cannot be requested back.

options.text: Azure allocates an address from its available pool.
options.explanation: The resource name does not reserve its former numeric address.

options.text: The resource starts with dynamic allocation until first use.
An unchanged DNS A record automatically tracks the new address.
options.explanation: A manually managed A record must be updated when its target changes.

questions.prompt: You are creating a new Standard public IPv4 resource in the portal for a regional frontend. Which configuration is valid?

options.text: Choose dynamic allocation and a private subnet address.
options.explanation: Standard uses static public allocation, outside the subnet's private pool.

options.text: Enter any unused public IPv4 address as its allocation.
options.explanation: Azure allocates the numeric address from its pool.

options.text: Select Standard with static allocation and compatible region/zone settings.
options.explanation: These settings match the supported creation model.

options.text: Create a DNS label instead of allocating a public IP.
options.explanation: The label is an optional property of the address resource.
